known_open_regression.scope: Research baseline only: copied detain restrictions are lost; no fix or full-support claim
known_open_regression.observation: Azure Mage is cast with real mana, waits a turn cycle and can activate before detain. Paid Inaction Injunction detains it and blocks native ability admission in the original game. In both snapshot modes the copy loses the flag, admits the ability and reports an omitted player-bound cleanup callback. The test fails at copied native admission before its future deadline checks. An earlier unused-import checkstyle failure is excluded.

positive_controls: Original timed cleanup already works; active death replacement and replay-to-exile already have correct visible outcomes in baseline snapshots but report omitted callbacks. These diagnostic cases are not called failed gameplay rules.

limits: Controlled partial four-player boards. Twenty-four paired native cases run both stack-copy modes; two replayed-spell cases use stack copying, and two original LKI contracts do not copy a game.
The two scheme-only native helper contracts use the variant-card registry. They are not normal Commander admission or scheme-rule certification; packaged witnesses use legal cards only.
Twelve packaged witnesses retain paid costs, card IDs/zones, raw regeneration counts and LKI values, effect-card inventories, native token/life outcomes and source/copy independence.
Fog uses a paid creature that waits a turn cycle. Its attacker declaration is controlled, followed by native triggers, blocker decisions and combat damage; general attacker policy is not certified.

Torrential Gearhulk stages a naturally replayed Opt on the stack. The copy resolves or counters it using a native legal spell target and actual counterspell costs. Existing move-trigger cleanup removes the effect before its idempotent end-of-turn callback.

Regeneration quotas are distinct from shield counters. Other combat-regeneration cases, replacement ordering, shield-counter interactions, subtype/controller variants, rollback and replay permissions remain unverified.
The source and LKI regeneration-history fixes copy raw state without performing regeneration or changing ordinary copiable characteristics.

Other callbacks, hidden/merged/perpetual state, arbitrary continuations and general AI policy remain incomplete. Unmapped diagnostics are asserted in fixtures, not aggregated into normal simulation reports.

Catalog construction proves script availability rather than full gameplay correctness. Seven unavailable entries are nonstarting meld results. Versioned references are not a complete current-rules audit.
